obligations.evidence: Code: every reveal calls EffectiveExplorerView -> ReadExplorerView -> SHGetSetSettings(..., false) again (ShellReveal.cs:346-361), and the app caches nothing. Measured in attempt 2: shell32 keeps the view cached in each process. In a WPF process with a DispatcherTimer and a new STA thread per read, a change to the underlying (private-hive) values went unseen for 3.8 s, over 15 reads. So a running app sees new settings only if Explorer's own Apply clears that cache. Only a person can toggle Explorer's settings, so that was not exercised. PERSON-RUN, all in one app session: (1) Start artifacts\publish\FsAnalyser.App.exe on a temp folder holding a file set with attrib +h +s, and reveal it. The status line must read "Nothing was opened: Explorer hides '<name>' (Hide protected operating system files)." (2) Without closing the app, untick 'Hide protected operating system files' in File Explorer Options > View, then press Apply. (3) Reveal the same row again. Explorer must open the folder with the file selected, and the status line must be empty. (4) Tick the option again, press Apply, and reveal again; it must be refused again. Repeat with View > Show > Hidden items for a file set with +h only.
